# Keenable web tools

Two tools are registered by the `opencode-keenable` plugin. Both work with no API
key; `KEENABLE_API_KEY` only raises the rate limits.

| Need | Tool |
|------|------|
| Find pages on a topic, answer a question from the web | `keenable_search` |
| Read a specific URL as markdown | `keenable_fetch` |

## keenable_search

Describe the ideal page in natural language rather than typing bare keywords:
`"changelog for the 2.x release of <library>"` beats `"<library> changelog"`.

Optional narrowing: `site` (one domain), `published_after` / `published_before`
(when the page was published), `acquired_after` / `acquired_before` (when Keenable
indexed it). All dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Results come back as JSON with `title`, `url` and `description`. They are a map,
not a source: open the promising ones with `keenable_fetch` before relying on a
claim or quoting anything.

## keenable_fetch

Takes one `http(s)` URL and returns the page's main content as markdown, along
with title, description, author and publication date. Use it after a search, or
directly whenever the user hands you a URL.

Private and internal hosts (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local, cloud metadata
endpoints) are refused before the request is sent.

## Rate limits

Keyless requests are rate-limited per IP. If a call reports the keyless limit,
tell the user they can create a key at <https://keenable.ai/console> and export
`KEENABLE_API_KEY`; do not silently retry in a loop.

# opencode-keenable

OpenCode plugin for [Keenable](https://keenable.ai) — web search and page fetch
for your agent, **keyless by default**. No signup, no CLI to install, no login
step: add one line to your config and the tools are there.

## Installation

Add the plugin to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-keenable"]
}
```

That is the whole setup. OpenCode installs the plugin with Bun on startup and
the tools work immediately against Keenable's public endpoints.

## Tools

| Tool | Use when |
|------|----------|
| `keenable_search` | No URL yet — find pages, check current events, read changelogs and API references |
| `keenable_fetch` | You have a URL — pull the page as clean markdown |

`keenable_search` takes a natural-language `query` and optional `site`,
`published_after` / `published_before`, `acquired_after` / `acquired_before`
(all dates `YYYY-MM-DD`). `keenable_fetch` takes one `http(s)` `url` and returns
the main content as markdown plus title, description, author and publication date.

## Configuration

Both are optional.

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `KEENABLE_API_KEY` | Switches to the authenticated endpoints, which raises the rate limits. Create a key at [keenable.ai/console](https://keenable.ai/console). |
| `KEENABLE_API_URL` | Base-URL override. HTTPS is enforced (plain http only for loopback). |

Keyless requests are rate-limited per IP. Without a key everything still works;
the key is a limit lift, not a prerequisite. Both variables are also forwarded to
shell commands run in the session.

## Notes

- Shipped as TypeScript. OpenCode runs plugins with Bun, so there is no build step.
- One dependency, `@opencode-ai/plugin`, for the `tool()` helper and its Zod
  schemas. The API calls themselves use `fetch` and the Node standard library.
- `keenable_fetch` refuses private and internal targets (loopback, RFC-1918,
  link-local, cloud metadata hosts) before sending the request.
- Errors from the API (rate limit, auth, bad input) come back as tool output
  rather than exceptions, so a failed lookup does not break the session.
